title: Positional encodings in 2D and 3D
hook: Attention can't see order. Sine tables added to tokens and rotations from coordinates are how a token learns where it is.

verified.claim: The 1D table uses omega = 1/10000^(i/(D/2)), with sine then cosine.
The lab's table matched that function on a CPU: gap 0 at width 8, 3.9e-16 at width 32.
PixArt divides its grid by a scale.
FLUX builds img_ids of time, row, column.
Wan's axis widths are computed from the head width.
Everything in the tables comes from this lesson's lab.

unchecked: We did not measure structure drift at off-trained sizes; the warning rests on the mechanism, not a render.
We did not check every model's table type. The list names only the ones we read.
